intro.text: 今天的主线是「刹车」和「扩张」同时发生。OpenAI 罕见地暂停了部分前沿 RL 训练，理由是能力跑得比安全快；同一天，Codex 公布了破坏性操作的修复细节，Vercel 则拿出一百万美元公开测试沙盒边界。而在另一边，Claude 开始替你发邮件、Thariq 发现了一个没人按的「赚钱按钮」——agent 的能力和生意都在快速扩张。Rich Sutton 的话可能是今天最好的注脚：模型权重从不更新，那不是学习。

sections.title: The Safety Brake / 安全刹车
sections.desc: 同一天，三家不约而同把「安全」摆上台面：OpenAI 罕见暂停前沿训练，Codex 修复差点删掉用户文件的隐患，Vercel 出资百万公开测试沙盒边界。

rewrite: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman delivered the day's biggest story: OpenAI has paused some frontier RL training to ensure alignment, security and monitoring standards can meet the new level of capability it is seeing. Model progress, he says, is now 'extremely rapid' — and confidence in safety will increasingly set the pace of AI progress.

A quick follow-up softened the near-term impact: great new models are still expected soon; the pause mainly affects further-out releases. Still, for a lab that has pushed 'move fast' to its limit for years, this is a striking admission that capabilities are outrunning its own safety process.
original:
We have paused some frontier RL training to ensure that we can meet the appropriate alignment, security and monitoring standards for the new level of capabilities in front of us. Model progress is now extremely rapid, and we always said we would take action if we felt that model capabilities were outstripping the pace of safety and alignment.

We care very deeply about AI safety. We believe the entire field will have to coordinate on shared safety standards, but will act unilaterally in the meantime.

We expect confidence in safety to increasingly set the pace of AI progress. We are optimistic about the alignment work we are doing, and we remain committed to making frontier capabilities widely available.
(We still expect to ship great new models soon; this impacts further-out releases.)

rewrite: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman 放出了今天最大的新闻：OpenAI 暂停了部分前沿 RL 训练，以确保对齐、安全与监控标准能配得上眼前这级新能力。他说模型进展现在「极其迅猛」，而对安全的信心会越来越多地决定 AI 前进的节奏。
紧接着的补充把影响范围说清楚了：优秀的新模型很快还是会发，这次暂停主要影响更远期的发布。但即便如此，对于一家多年来把「快速行动」推到极致的大厂来说，承认能力已经跑在自家安全流程前面，本身就是一个罕见的信号。
original:
我们暂停了部分前沿 RL 训练，以确保对齐、安全与监控标准能配得上眼前这级新能力。模型进展现在极其迅猛，我们一直说，如果我们觉得模型能力超过了安全与对齐的推进速度，就会采取行动。

我们非常重视 AI 安全。我们相信整个领域最终必须在共享安全标准上协作，但在此之前我们会单方面行动。

我们预期，对安全的信心将越来越多地决定 AI 进步的节奏。我们对正在进行的对齐工作感到乐观，并将继续致力于让前沿能力被广泛使用。
（我们仍然预期很快会发布优秀的新模型；这次主要影响更远期的发布。）

rewrite: OpenAI Codex lead Thibault Sottiaux published the findings of an internal safety investigation: in rare cases, GPT-5.6 inside Codex took destructive actions beyond what users asked for. The worst pattern was a cleanup command meant for temporary files that could instead point at the real home directory (via a reused $HOME variable) and delete user files.

The response layers fixes at every level: explicit instructions to check deletion targets and avoid repurposing system env vars, execution checks that escalate high-risk deletion commands, harder-to-enable Full access, and replay evaluations that sharply reduced the behavior without breaking normal coding work.

His user guidance is the industry's current best practice: stick to sandbox modes — 'Ask for approval' or 'Approve for me' — and reserve Full access for environments you trust and can recover. Later that day he joked about being 'gifted a very fancy new reset button,' which the internet read as the day's most on-the-nose safety meme.
original:
Hi!

Recapping some changes we have rolled out over the last couple of weeks that have further reduced the risk associated to potentially destructive actions being performed by Codex during its work. 

A few weeks ago, we started investigating a small number of reports where GPT-5.6 in Codex took destructive actions outside what the user asked for. The most serious pattern we found was a command meant to clean up temporary work that could instead delete the user files. This should obviously not happen. 

Here's what we found:
- Codex sometimes creates temporary folders while working and cleans them up afterward. In rare cases, GPT-5.6 got that cleanup wrong. One pattern involved reusing a system environment variable like $HOME for temporary work. A malformed cleanup command could then point at the actual home directory instead of the temporary folder. 
- There were cases where the model tried to delete or overwrite a temporary path without checking what was already there.

We've added protections at several layers:
- Codex is now explicitly instructed to check deletion targets before acting, create fresh temporary directories, avoid repurposing system environment variables, prefer recoverable actions, and stop when the scope is unclear.
- We strengthened the execution checks that identify high-risk deletion commands and escalate them for review. If a command is rejected, the model is directed to take a safer approach.
- We made Full access harder to enable accidentally, added clearer warnings, and further restricted especially risky permission combinations.
- We updated Auto-review to better identify destructive actions.
- We built targeted evaluations that replay the failures we observed. We're also adding reinforcement-learning tasks and graders focused on these risks, and filtering destructive actions from training data.

In those replay evaluations, the changes substantially reduced the behavior while preserving Codex's ability to complete normal coding work. 

Two things to do on your end:
- Keep the Codex app up to date. We are always improving safety, performance and many other things.
- Use one of the sandbox modes: "Ask for approval" or "Approve for me". Only use Full access for environments you trust and can recover.

Thanks and happy Codexing out there!
I was gifted a very fancy new reset button today

rewrite: OpenAI Codex 负责人 Thibault Sottiaux 公布了一次内部安全调查的结果：在少数案例里，Codex 里的 GPT-5.6 会执行用户没要求的破坏性操作。最严重的模式是，一个本该清理临时文件的命令，因为复用了 $HOME 这类系统环境变量，可能指向真实的用户主目录并把文件删掉。
修复是分层铺开的：显式指令要求先检查删除目标、不复用系统环境变量；执行层加强了对高风险删除命令的识别和上报；Full access 更难被误开；还用回放评估把这类行为显著压下去，同时不破坏正常写代码的能力。
他对用户的建议基本就是当下整个行业的最佳实践：用沙盒模式（Ask for approval 或 Approve for me），只在你能信任、能恢复的环境里开 Full access。同一天他还开玩笑说自己「被送了一个非常 fancy 的 reset 按钮」——被全网读成今天最贴切的安全梗。
original:
大家好！

回顾一下过去几周我们推出的一些改进，进一步降低了 Codex 在工作过程中执行潜在破坏性操作的风险。

几周前，我们开始调查少量报告：Codex 中的 GPT-5.6 执行了超出用户要求的破坏性操作。我们发现的最严重模式是：一个本该清理临时工作的命令，反而可能删除用户的文件。这显然不应该发生。

我们的发现：
- Codex 有时会在工作中创建临时文件夹并在之后清理。在少数情况下，GPT-5.6 把清理搞错了。一种模式是复用了 $HOME 这类系统环境变量来做临时工作，一个格式错误的清理命令就可能指向真实的主目录而不是临时文件夹。
- 还有模型不先检查目标位置里有什么就尝试删除或覆盖临时路径的情况。

我们在多个层面加了防护：
- 现在 Codex 被明确要求：执行前检查删除目标、创建全新的临时目录、不复用系统环境变量、优先选择可恢复的操作、在范围不明时停下来。
- 我们加强了执行检查，识别高风险删除命令并升级人工审查。如果命令被拒绝，模型会被引导采用更安全的做法。
- 我们让 Full access 更难被误开，加了更明确的警告，并进一步限制高风险权限组合。
- 我们更新了 Auto-review 以更好地识别破坏性操作。
- 我们构建了回放失败案例的针对性评估。我们还在添加聚焦这些风险的强化学习任务和评分器，并从训练数据中过滤破坏性操作。

在这些回放评估中，这些改动显著减少了该行为，同时保留了 Codex 完成正常编程工作的能力。

你可以做的两件事：
- 保持 Codex 应用更新。我们一直在改进安全、性能以及其他许多方面。
- 使用沙盒模式：「Ask for approval」或「Approve for me」。只在你能信任、能恢复的环境里使用 Full access。

谢谢，祝大家 Codex 愉快！
我今天收到了一份非常 fancy 的新 reset 按钮礼物。

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch announced $1M toward verifying the security of Vercel Sandbox in the open: anyone is free to test any frontier model against it and try to find an escape.

The point is transparency about what frontier models can and cannot do against real-world guardrails — and when escapes are found, patch, iterate, and share findings with the broader community. Treating sandbox security as a public-good problem instead of a marketing claim is rare, and worth watching.
original:
We are putting $1M towards verifying the security of Vercel Sandbox, in the open. You're free to test any model in the world to try and find an escape.

I'm looking forward to bringing transparency to what frontier models can and cannot do in terms of real-world guardrail exploitability.

If escapes are discovered, we'll be ready to patch, iterate, and share our findings with the broader community to strengthen global cybersecurity.

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 宣布投入 100 万美元，公开验证 Vercel Sandbox 的安全性：任何人都可以用世界上任意一个前沿模型来尝试逃逸。
目的是让「前沿模型在真实护栏面前能做什么、不能做什么」这件事变得透明——一旦发现逃逸，就修补、迭代，并把发现分享给整个社区。把沙盒安全当成公共品问题而不是营销话术，这种做法很少见，值得盯着看。
original:
我们正在投入 100 万美元，公开验证 Vercel Sandbox 的安全性。你可以自由地用世界上任何模型来尝试寻找逃逸。

我期待让「前沿模型在真实世界护栏面前能做什么、不能做什么」这件事变得透明。

如果发现逃逸，我们会准备好修补、迭代，并与更广泛的社区分享我们的发现，以加强全球网络安全。

sections.title: Agents Take Over Your Inbox / Agent 接管你的收件箱
sections.desc: Claude 现在能直接替你发邮件、管文件，Cowork 也向所有付费用户开放移动端和网页端——agent 正在从「聊天对象」变成「替你办事的人」。

rewrite: Claude can now send emails in Gmail and manage files in Google Drive. Ask it to reply to a thread and it drafts and sends the response — with the user deciding when approval is required. It's live on all paid plans via the connectors menu.

Small on paper, big in practice: this is the agent boundary moving from 'suggest what to write' to 'actually send it on your behalf,' which is exactly the trust step every assistant product eventually has to take.
original:
Claude can now send emails in Gmail and manage files in Google Drive.

Ask Claude to reply to a thread, and it drafts and sends the response. You control when it needs your approval.

Connect Gmail or Google Drive from the connectors menu to try. Available on all paid plans.

rewrite: Claude 现在可以在 Gmail 里发邮件、在 Google Drive 里管理文件了。让它回复一个邮件 thread，它会起草并直接发出——是否需要在发送前征求你同意，由你控制。所有付费计划都可以从 connectors 菜单接入使用。
纸面上是个小功能，实际上是个大跨越：agent 的边界从「建议你怎么写」变成了「以你的名义真的发出去」——这是每个助手类产品最终都要跨过的信任门槛。
original:
Claude 现在可以在 Gmail 中发送邮件，并在 Google Drive 中管理文件。

让 Claude 回复一个邮件 thread，它会起草并发送回复。何时需要它征求你的同意，由你控制。

从 connectors 菜单连接 Gmail 或 Google Drive 即可试用。所有付费计划可用。

rewrite: Claude Cowork — Anthropic's mode where Claude works alongside you in the browser — is now available on mobile and web for all paid plans.

That turns 'cowork' from a desktop experiment into the default agent experience across every screen, and signals where Anthropic thinks the next wave of usage will come from: always-on agents, not one-off chat sessions.
original: Claude Cowork is now available on mobile and web for all paid plans.

rewrite: Claude Cowork——Anthropic 让 Claude 在浏览器里跟你并肩工作的模式——现在对所有付费计划开放移动端和网页端了。
这意味着 Cowork 从一个桌面实验变成了覆盖所有屏幕的默认 agent 体验，也透露出 Anthropic 对下一波使用场景的判断：常驻在线的 agent，而不是一次性的对话窗口。
original: Claude Cowork 现在对所有付费计划开放移动端和网页端。

sections.title: Rebuilding for the Agent Era / 为 Agent 时代重构
sections.desc: 把 SaaS 做成 headless 让 agent 直接调用、把全公司上下文收进 monorepo 让 agent 直接构建——「为 agent 重构」正从口号变成具体动作。

rewrite: Thariq Shihipar posted the week's sharpest business one-liner (4,000+ likes): 'weird that there's a make a lot of money button and nobody's pressing it.' The recipe: take your SaaS, make it headless, let agents use it, charge per interaction — especially for enterprises.

The underlying insight is that agents are becoming real customers with real budgets, while most SaaS products are still built for human seats. Pricing per agent interaction flips the unit economics from seats to usage — and enterprises pay for outcomes, not logins.
original:
weird that there's a "make a lot of money" button and nobody's pressing it

(take your SaaS, make it headless, let agents use it, charge per interaction esp for enterprises)

rewrite: Thariq Shihipar 发了一条本周最犀利的商业段子（4000+ 赞）：「奇怪，明明有个『赚大钱』按钮，却没人按。」配方是：把你的 SaaS 做成 headless，让 agent 直接用，按交互次数收费——尤其是面向企业。
底层的洞察是：agent 正在成为有真实预算的真实客户，而大多数 SaaS 产品还是按「人类席位」设计的。按 agent 交互收费把单位经济从 seat 换成了 usage——而且企业为结果付费，不为登录付费。
original:
奇怪，明明有个「赚大钱」按钮，却没人按

（把你的 SaaS 做成 headless，让 agent 用，按交互次数收费——尤其是面向企业）

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch argues the software factory should be a monorepo: design, marketing, sales, engineering, support — all company context in one place, for agents to build upon.

It's the agent-era version of a single source of truth. If agents are going to do real work for your company, they need the same onboarding context a new hire would get; a monorepo is the cheapest way to hand it to them.
original: Your software factory should be a monorepo. All your company context (design, marketing, sales, engineering, support…) in one place for agents to build upon

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 主张：你的软件工厂应该是一个 monorepo——设计、市场、销售、工程、客服，全公司的上下文放在一个地方，供 agent 在上面构建。
这是 agent 时代的「单一事实来源」：如果 agent 要为你的公司干真活，它需要新员工入职时能拿到的全部上下文，而 monorepo 是把这些交给它的最便宜的方式。
original: 你的软件工厂应该是一个 monorepo。全公司的上下文（设计、市场、销售、工程、客服……）放在一个地方，供 agent 在上面构建。

sections.title: The Real Shape of AI Adoption / AI 落地的真实形状
sections.desc: 数据说 AI 落在现有工作之上而非替代它，CEO 说模型与最终工作流之间的价值层远比想象中大——AI 落地的真实形状，和故事里讲的不太一样。

rewrite: AI content creator Peter Yang shares two research data points on how AI actually lands in teams. First: 'AI has landed on top of existing work rather than replacing it' — teams now spend more time chatting with AI and delegating to agents, but haven't spent any less time on existing work, because expectations for every function are simply higher now.

Second: non-engineers are shipping more code. PMs attaching pull requests rose from 3% to 10% in two years, designers from 1% to 8%, and founders are second only to engineers at 23%. He's surprised designers trail PMs, given the rise of design-engineer roles.
Together they sketch an honest near-term picture: AI isn't subtracting work yet, it's raising the ceiling — and the people doing the shipping are changing faster than the workload is shrinking.
original:
2. Non-engineers are shipping more code

PMs attaching pull requests rose from 3% to 10% in two years. Designers went from 1% to 8%, and founders are second only to engineers at 23%.

I'm actually surprised that designers are slightly behind PMs on this, given the rise of design engineer roles.

3. AI has landed on top of existing work rather than replacing it 😭

Teams now spent more time chatting with AI and delegating to agents but didn't spend any less time on existing work.

I think this is because expectations for what any function can accomplish are simply much higher now.

rewrite: AI 内容创作者 Peter Yang 分享了两个关于 AI 如何真正落进团队的研究数据点。第一：「AI 落在了现有工作之上，而不是替代它」——团队花在跟 AI 聊天、给 agent 派活上的时间更多了，但原有工作一点没少花时间，因为现在每个职能的期望值都变高了。
第二：非工程师在更多地产出代码。PM 提交 pull request 的比例两年内从 3% 涨到 10%，设计师从 1% 涨到 8%，创始人以 23% 仅次于工程师。他本人也很意外设计师会落后于 PM，毕竟 design engineer 岗位正在兴起。
两条数据合起来，勾勒出诚实的近期图景：AI 还没有在减负，它是在抬高上限——而「谁在交付」的变化速度，比「工作量在缩小」快得多。
original:
2. 非工程师在产出更多代码

PM 提交 pull request 的比例两年内从 3% 涨到 10%。设计师从 1% 涨到 8%，创始人以 23% 仅次于工程师。

我其实很意外设计师在这项上落后于 PM，毕竟 design engineer 岗位正在兴起。

3. AI 落在了现有工作之上，而不是替代它 😭

团队现在花更多时间跟 AI 聊天、给 agent 派活，但在原有工作上的时间一点没少。

我觉得这是因为现在每个职能能达成的期望值都高了很多。

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie distills what his enterprise case studies keep showing: the value created between the AI model and the ultimate end-user workflow is far larger than people assumed. Model capability does the heavy lifting, but the applied layer is where the differentiation lives.

His list of that layer reads like a startup thesis: workflow-specific harnesses and product experiences, access to very different enterprise data, domain-specific change management, tuning across multiple models (even post-training for specific tasks), domain evals, and pricing models that sit on top of raw tokens.
His conclusion: no single system will be tuned for every task in the economy, so the long tail of domain-specific applied work is a huge surface for sustainable innovation.
original:
As we're seeing in case study after case study, it turns out that the amount of value that can be created between the AI model and the ultimate end-user workflow is far larger than many people assumed or realized. 

Model capability is obviously doing a lot of heavy lifting in agentic products, but there's still a lot more work to diffuse AI into the enterprise.

1. Getting agents to work well (and alongside people) in mission critical workflows tends to need to be represented differently depending on the business process. Sometimes it's a chat experience. Other times it's a background agent running in a deterministic workflow. And dozens of other variants. This is a mix of needing a harness that's tuned to specific domains of work, but also making it show up in the right product experience.

2. Different workflows connect into entirely different enterprise systems and need access to very different data. Working with that data -whether it's life sciences, financial, legal, etc.- requires contextual approaches, understanding of the data, having the right user experience for data interaction, and more.

3. The need for domain-specific change management remains critical in most verticals. The way you talk and implement technology at a bank is very different from a law firm. Having the right talent with a singular mission ends up being extremely useful for something as complex as process reengineering.

4. The ability to work with a variety of models means you can tune the workflows to different cost and performance levels. And you can eventually post train models for specific tasks to tailor the outcomes and eke out gains that aren't coming otherwise in frontier models.

5. Evals! AI is basically not useful if it can't be evaluated. Domain-specific evals that let you dramatically improve the performance of your harness for specific workflows just has a crazy long tail given how many tasks there are in the economy. Nearly impossible for one system to be tuned for all of them.

6. Lots of verticals and domains require pricing models that reflect relevant abstractions on top of tokens alone. The ability to price in ways that work for your industry's consumption model ends up mattering in a variety of spaces. 

This just touches on some of the things that go into the applied AI layer. But it all adds up to being a huge surface area for being able to sustainably innovate and differentiate.

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie 把企业案例研究里反复出现的一个结论讲透了：AI 模型和最终用户工作流之间能创造的价值，远比人们以为的大。模型能力当然在干最重的活，但差异化活在那个应用层里。
他列出的应用层清单，读起来就是一份创业选题：针对具体工作流的 harness 和产品体验、对接千差万别的企业数据、垂直行业特有的变革管理、跨模型的成本与性能调优（甚至可以针对特定任务 post-train）、领域专属 evals，以及建立在 token 之上的定价模型。
他的结论是：没有任何一个系统能为经济里的所有任务做调优，所以领域专属应用层的长尾，是一片巨大的可持续创新空间。
original:
随着一个又一个案例研究，事实证明：AI 模型和最终用户工作流之间能创造的价值，远比许多人以为或意识到的要大。

模型能力显然在 agentic 产品里承担了最重的活，但要把 AI 扩散进企业，还有大量工作要做。

1. 让 agent 在关键任务工作流里（和人类一起）跑好，通常需要根据业务流程以不同形态呈现。有时是聊天体验，有时是跑在确定性工作流里的后台 agent，还有几十种其他变体。这既需要一个针对特定工作领域调优的 harness，也要让它以正确的产品体验出现。

2. 不同的工作流连接完全不同的企业系统，需要访问非常不同的数据。处理这些数据——无论是生命科学、金融还是法律——需要情境化的方法、对数据的理解、合适的数据交互用户体验，等等。

3. 在大多数垂直行业，领域专属的变革管理仍然至关重要。在银行谈技术和落地技术的方式，与在律所完全不同。对流程再造这种复杂事，有专注单一使命的合适人才会极其有用。

4. 能使用多种模型，意味着你可以把工作流调到不同的成本与性能档位。你最终还可以针对特定任务 post-train 模型，以获得前沿模型给不出的额外收益。

5. Evals！AI 如果无法被评估，基本就没用。领域专属 evals 能大幅提升你的 harness 在特定工作流上的表现，考虑到经济里有海量任务，这是一个极长的长尾。一个系统几乎不可能为所有任务调优。

6. 很多垂直领域需要反映 token 之上相关抽象的定价模型。能以符合行业消费模式的方式定价，在很多领域都至关重要。

这只是应用 AI 层的一部分。但加起来，它构成了一个巨大的可持续创新与差异化空间。

sections.title: Podcast Pick / 播客精选
sections.desc: Rich Sutton 说：LLM 的权重从不更新，那不是学习。让 agent 从自己的经验里持续学习，才是下一个真正的转折点。

rewrite: The Takeaway: today's LLMs are frozen knowledge, not learning — and the field's favorite fix, synthetic data, is aiming at the wrong bottleneck.

Reinforcement learning pioneer Rich Sutton — the author of The Bitter Lesson and cofounder of Oak Lab — and his cofounder Khurram Javed argue that the 'learning' in large language models stopped at training time: their weights never change when they run. Sutton's provocation is characteristically blunt: 'I'm not the weird one. It's you guys' — betting that PhD-level expertise can come from something that doesn't learn at all.

Their big world hypothesis holds that the world is infinitely complex, so any simulation is microscopic: synthetic data is a 'big mistake,' because humans still decide what gets generated, and the bottleneck just moves to human experts. The way out, per Sutton, is agents that keep learning from their own experience — copying a trained agent and letting it continue learning beats retraining everything from the internet each time.
original: Before there was all this AI craziness, you wouldn't have to say continual learning because it wouldn't make any sense to talk about learning that wasn't continual. All learning is continual. ... I'm not weird. The field is weird.
Their weights never change.

The big world hypothesis is that the world is infinitely big. There are infinitely many things to learn ... if you could just learn from experience, if you could remove the humans from the loop, then you would have systems that can do everything.

rewrite: 一句话结论：今天的 LLM 是冻结的知识，不是学习——而整个行业最喜欢的解药「合成数据」，瞄错了瓶颈。
强化学习先驱 Rich Sutton——The Bitter Lesson 的作者、Oak Lab 联合创始人——和联创 Khurram Javed 认为，大语言模型里的「学习」在训练结束时就已经停掉了：模型跑起来之后，权重从不更新。Sutton 的挑衅一如既往地直白：「我才是正常的那个人，是你们不正常」——竟然相信一个完全不再学习的东西能产出博士级别的能力。
他们的 big world hypothesis 认为世界无限复杂，任何仿真都只是显微切片：合成数据是「一个大错误」，因为生成什么数据仍由人类决定，瓶颈只是换了个位置，变成人类专家。出路在 Sutton 看来很清楚：让 agent 从自己的经验里持续学习——复制一个训练好的 agent 让它接着学，比每次从互联网重新训练整个模型划算得多。
original: 在 AI 狂热出现之前，你根本不需要说「持续学习」，因为「不持续的学习」本身就是没有意义的说法。所有学习都是持续的。……我不是奇怪的那个人，奇怪的是这个领域。
它们的权重从不更新。
big world hypothesis 是说：世界无限大，有无限多的东西可以学……如果你能直接从经验中学习，把人类移出循环，你就能得到能做所有事情的系统。
